runtime_proof.note: Measured read-only against production zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm. No row was written, updated or deleted; no containment setting, kill switch, delivery target or deploy was touched. This block establishes that the defect is real in production and that the waiver's current boundary is exactly where the code says it is -- it does not claim the repair is deployed.

queries.name: the event-existence gate is ARMED in production
queries.method: read-only SELECT count(*) FROM events, and count(*) WHERE event_date BETWEEN current_date - 90 AND current_date + 90
queries.result: 790 events total, 178 inside the window EventRepository.listUpcoming(undefined, 90) actually reads, 0 with event_date >= current_date, newest event_date 2026-09-17
queries.significance: checkEventExistenceGate returns early only when listUpcoming is empty. It is not empty, so the gate fires on every submission. The 178 are all expired -- listUpcoming is misnamed and reads today-90 through today+90 -- which is why an operator sees no selectable game and still meets an armed gate.

queries.name: every no-match submission that persisted is Track Only -- none is delivery-eligible
queries.method: read-only correlated count over picks WHERE metadata ? 'distributionMode', partitioned by distributionMode, counting those whose metadata.participantResolution.eventName matches ZERO rows in events (case-insensitive, the same comparison EventRepository.listByName makes)
queries.significance: This is the defect, measured rather than argued. The UTV2-1842 waiver demonstrably works -- five Track Only picks naming no catalogued event are persisted in production. Not one delivery-eligible pick is, because the waiver excluded that caller. UTV2-1923 pins an allow-listed capper to delivery-eligible, so that caller is precisely the one who cannot submit.

queries.name: the one delivery-eligible pick that DID persist had a real event match, so it never needed the waiver
queries.method: read-only join of the four newest governed picks against events on lower(event_name)
queries.result: 816a84c7 (delivery-eligible, 'Lions @ Bills') -> 1 matching event row. b7b34a7f (track-only, 'Lions @ Bills') -> 1. 5c527e5e (track-only, 'Padres @ Rockies') -> 0. 04174f12 (track-only, 'Broncos @ Chiefs') -> 0.
queries.significance: Rules out the alternative explanation that delivery-eligible submissions work fine. The only one that succeeded satisfied the gate outright; the two that needed the waiver were both Track Only. A delivery-eligible submission naming no catalogued event has never persisted in this database.

queries.name: submission has stopped since the last event match expired
queries.method: read-only count of picks created in the last 24 hours
queries.result: 3 governed picks in the last 24h, the newest at 2026-09-18 01:36:52Z; none since
queries.significance: Consistent with a pre-persistence refusal rather than a partial write: the operator's later attempts produced no row at all, which is what a 422 at submission-service.ts before any insert looks like from the database side.

queries.name: containment is unchanged by this proof
queries.method: read-only SELECT target, killed FROM delivery_kill_switch
queries.result: best-bets=true, exclusive-insights=true, official-picks=true, trader-insights=true (t1-proof-utv2-1427-kill-switch=false is a test fixture target, not a governed one)
queries.significance: Every governed delivery target is killed, before and after this proof. The repair admits a pick to persistence; it grants no delivery, and the control that would have to be released to deliver one is untouched.

observations.what: the defect is a collision between two correct lanes, not a defect in either
observations.evidence: UTV2-1842's predicate was exact when written, because handlers/submit-pick.ts pinned every authenticated capper to track-only. UTV2-1923 changed the pin for an allow-listed capper to delivery-eligible. Neither diff is wrong in isolation; the 0-vs-5 partition above is what the pair produces together.

observations.what: the waiver's scope is persistence, not delivery
observations.evidence: all four governed delivery targets remain killed=true; the repair touches neither the registry target gate nor the kill switch, and the live-DB test asserts the delivery outcome in both directions rather than assuming one

observations.what: the authorization fact cannot be supplied by a client
observations.evidence: handlers/submit-pick.ts deletes humanCapperDeliveryAuthorizationKey off the incoming payload unconditionally on every branch, then re-authors it from the env allow-list and the authenticated identity; the malformed-record unit test asserts the reader refuses a forged copy

observations.what: a second, separate defect was found and deliberately NOT repaired here
observations.evidence: EventRepository.listUpcoming(sportId, windowDays) reads today-windowDays through today+windowDays, so 178 expired rows arm a gate named for upcoming events. Recorded rather than bundled into a lane whose stated purpose is something else.
